active_paradigms.idea: Lift the 3-fold ansatz and use one full-dimensional differential-evolution search over a convex-polygon hull parameterization
active_paradigms.description: The current program is strong because it exploits affine invariance, fixes an equilateral triangular hull, reduces the search to six 3-fold-symmetric variables, evaluates all 286 triangles exactly, and finally performs an epigraph SLSQP refinement. Its main limitation is structural: it requires exactly three prescribed hull vertices, a center point, and three rotational point orbits, so it cannot represent configurations with a non-triangular hull, broken symmetry, or uneven orbit geometry. Replace this restricted representation by a parameterization with, for example, 5--7 hull vertices described by sorted angles and positive radial values, plus interior points represented by convex combinations of that polygon's vertices. Use a single scipy.optimize.differential_evolution call on this parameterization, with a fixed seed and an objective equal to the actual minimum absolute determinant divided by the shoelace area of the parameterized hull. Canonicalize affine freedom by fixing three hull degrees of freedom, such as setting two vertices to (0,0) and (1,0) and fixing a third vertex's x-coordinate. Penalize invalid cyclic hulls, self-intersections, nearly zero hull area, and interior points outside the polygon. This directly searches oriented-matroid families unavailable to the current triangular/3-fold design and may discover that the best 13-point normalized configuration has more than three extreme points.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; specifically remove the current symmetry and triangular-hull restrictions while retaining exact evaluation of all 286 triangle areas. Runtime is controlled by a moderate population and fixed maximum generation count.
active_paradigms.cautions: The evaluator has no unit-area or bounding-box constraint: only the ratio to ConvexHull area matters, so do not optimize raw areas or accidentally impose a scale penalty. The parameterized shoelace denominator must match the true ConvexHull area; enforce strict convex cyclic order so that it does. Differential evolution should be the only optimization call, rather than followed by a local optimizer, and its returned candidate should be rechecked with scipy.spatial.ConvexHull before caching.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a direct nonsmooth COBYLA epigraph solve with all 13 points free after affine gauge fixing
active_paradigms.description: The current local SLSQP stage has a useful epigraph formulation, but it freezes every triple orientation from a single symmetric incumbent and fixes the first three points as the equilateral hull. That can reject a better solution if a productive move crosses an orientation-change boundary or changes which points belong to the hull. Formulate one scipy.optimize.minimize call with method='COBYLA' over all free coordinates and an epigraph variable t, after fixing three noncollinear gauge points only to eliminate translation, rotation, and scale. Use inequality constraints |det(i,j,k)| - 2*t*A_hull >= 0 for every triple, represented as two signed determinant branches only within an explicitly selected oriented-matroid cell; choose the cell from a high-quality deterministic hand-designed configuration rather than the current forced 3-fold one. Keep the hull fixed to a chosen convex m-gon by expressing all non-gauge points in polygon barycentric coordinates, so A_hull is constant and the triangle constraints are clean. COBYLA is particularly appropriate because the maximin geometry has many active inequalities and derivative estimates of abs determinants become unreliable near equioscillation. A successful result should show many triangles tightly clustered at the achieved threshold, rather than one isolated small triangle. This is a fundamentally different local strategy from the current SLSQP refinement: optimize a less constrained, non-symmetric active-set cell directly rather than using global search followed by SLSQP.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Raise the bottleneck triangle threshold t while allowing all 13 locations to break 3-fold symmetry; optimize feasibility robustness and the primary normalized score, not raw hull area.
active_paradigms.cautions: COBYLA accepts only inequality constraints and can be sensitive to coordinate scale, so normalize the fixed hull to O(1) dimensions and set a sufficiently large maxiter/rhobeg. A fixed sign pattern is valid only while every determinant stays positive with margin; reject any final result whose actual absolute-area score is lower than its epigraph claim. The selected hull polygon must remain the actual hull, otherwise normalization in the evaluator differs from the constant denominator used in the optimization.

active_paradigms.idea: Use SHGO to enumerate and compare low-dimensional symmetry classes instead of committing to one 3-fold orbit topology
active_paradigms.description: The score of 0.731044 comes from a single 3-fold topology containing three hull vertices, one center, and three generic 3-point orbits. This is an excellent low-dimensional baseline, but the true best arrangement may belong to a different finite symmetry class, such as reflection symmetry with paired points, 6-fold partial symmetry, or threefold symmetry without a center point. For each candidate class, build a compact fundamental-domain parameterization that guarantees points lie in a fixed equilateral hull, and use one scipy.optimize.shgo call to maximize the exact minimum normalized triangle determinant in that class. SHGO's simplicial sampling is valuable here because it identifies distinct basins of the piecewise-smooth minimum-area landscape rather than repeatedly evolving one population toward the same basin. The most promising alternative classes for exactly 13 points are a reflection-symmetric 6+6 pair structure plus one point, and a 3-fold structure with one orbit constrained on each side but no forced centroid point. Select a single class based on deterministic preliminary geometric reasoning and make its SHGO result the constructor output; the function call itself remains deterministic. This attacks the current program's largest issue—an unverified symmetry topology—while retaining enough dimension for a global method to be credible.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary normalized minimum triangle area through discovery of a different symmetry/orbit topology; secondary objective is reproducibility because SHGO's sampling is deterministic under fixed bounds.
active_paradigms.cautions: SHGO scales poorly with dimension, so this is appropriate only for a deliberately low-dimensional orbit parameterization, not all 26 coordinates. Its objective is nonsmooth at changes in the active triangle; use dense enough simplicial sampling and evaluate the exact absolute determinants, not a surrogate that can alter rankings. As with the existing code, ensure all generated orbit points are inside the fixed hull and independently recompute all 286 triangle areas before returning.
